LESSON: SWIMMING (OPTIONAL)

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.5: Swimming (Optional)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Swimming (Optional), part of Performing and Displaying in Grade 6 CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why are swimming skills considered as survival skills?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch a virtual or actual performance to observe breaststroke in swimming,

2. demonstrate breaststroke skill,

3. practise breaststroke skills while observing safety,

4. apply the skill of breaststroke in swimming game,

5. observe each other swim using breaststroke and give feedback.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch a virtual or actual performance to observe breaststroke in swimming,
2. demonstrate breaststroke skill,
3. practise breaststroke skills while observing safety,
4. apply the skill of breaststroke in swimming game,
5. observe each other swim using breaststroke and give feedback.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Swimming (Optional) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: The learner expresses water confidence as they practise the skill of breaststroke and provide feedback to each

other about the performance.

• Learning to learn: The learner acquires new skill of breaststroke while practising in the swimming pool.

Values:
• Unity: The learner displays team spirit while applying the skills of breaststroke.

• Responsibility: The learner observes own and others’ safety while practising breaststroke.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety: The learner observes safety measures as they practise breaststroke during swimming.

• Life skills: The learner acquires swimming skills as survival skills in case of emergencies such as floods.

Link to other learning areas:

Integrated Science: The learner uses the knowledge of floatation to perform breaststroke in swimming..
